questions.prompt: Match each status code family to its meaning.
questions.explanation: 1xx is informational, 2xx success, 3xx redirection, 4xx client error, and 5xx server error.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between HTTP 401 and 403?

options.text: 401 = not authenticated; 403 = authenticated but not allowed

questions.explanation: 401 Unauthorized means you must authenticate; 403 Forbidden means you are known but not permitted to do this.

questions.prompt: Which statements about HTTP methods are correct? Select all that apply.

options.text: DELETE is idempotent but not safe
POST is neither safe nor idempotent
Safe and idempotent always mean the same thing

questions.explanation: GET is safe+idempotent, DELETE is idempotent but changes state, POST is neither. Safe and idempotent are independent properties.

questions.prompt: HTTP is stateless, so continuity between requests is added with a token the server sets and the browser returns — a ____.
questions.explanation: The server sends Set-Cookie and the browser returns the Cookie header on later requests, tying them to a session.

questions.prompt: Why is blindly retrying a timed-out POST risky?

options.text: POST is not idempotent, so the retry may repeat side effects (e.g. a double charge)
POST requests are always rejected on retry

questions.explanation: POST is not idempotent, so a retry can duplicate its effect. Idempotency keys or an idempotent method make retries safe.

questions.prompt: Order the parts of an HTTP request from first to last.
questions.explanation: An HTTP message is a start line, headers, a blank line, then an optional body.
